newsitem.title: FINLAND: POLAR TO RAISE NEW CAPITAL, CONVERT DEBT.
newsitem.headline: POLAR TO RAISE NEW CAPITAL, CONVERT DEBT.

text.p: Finnish construction group Polar-Yhtyma Oy said in a statement on Friday it would issue new shares, convertible bonds and bonds for a maximum of 2.4 billion markka in total.

The issues would the group's equity to assets ratio above 31 percent from 15.7 and the group's largest creditors had committed to convert current instruments for new ones issued for over 950 million markka, it said.
"The maximum amount of the share issue is 1,000,000,000 markka. The subscription price is ten markka," it said.
The maximum issue amount of convertible bonds was 800 million markka and the maximum of bonds was 600 million.
The arrangement is part of one to convert bonds with warrants issued in 1994 to other instruments, it said.

Cervuctum Oy, an investment company owned by Metra, UPM-Kymmene, Partek and SOK, earlier this autumn acquired a large stake in Polar through warrants and bonds with warrants and said it would start talks to improve Polar's capital structure.
The convertible bonds now issued would mature on December 31 2046 but Polar has the right to repay it earlier, Polar said. They were uncollateralised and would not be listed, it said.
Every 1,000 markka of outstanding capital of the bonds could be converted for 100 Polar shares.
Of the bonds -- also not he be publicly traded -- 10 percent would mature on December 31, 2001 and 30 percent in each of the years 2002 to 2004, Polar said. It did not state the coupon payment.
